## Overview

Before normalizing drug responses or fitting dose-response models, it is critical to verify that cell segmentation, marker classification, and replicate fields of view (series) behaved consistently across your microscopy screen.

This tutorial demonstrates the complete quality control (QC) workflow in `drugsens`:

1. Auditing per-image total cell counts (`sum_cells`) and marker ratios with `make_count_dataframe()`.
2. Visualizing patient-level marker positivity distributions and testing treatments against `Control` with `get_QC_plots()`.
3. Comparing marker ratios across tissue origins and drug concentrations with `get_QC_plots_parsed_merged_data()`.
4. Inspecting single-cell morphological features (such as nuclear area and marker intensity) directly from `data_binding()`.

---

## 1. Auditing Image-Level Cell Counts and Marker Ratios

First, bind the example QuPath CSV files and compute image-level counts using `make_count_dataframe()`:

```{r qc-step1}
library(drugsens)

example_dir <- system.file("extdata/to_merge/", package = "drugsens")
bind_data <- data_binding(
  path_to_the_projects_folder = example_dir,
  files_extension_to_look_for = "csv"
)

counts_df <- make_count_dataframe(bind_data)
summary(counts_df[, c("sum_cells", "cCASP3_ratio_of_total_cells",
                      "E-Cadherin_ratio_of_total_cells", "onlyDAPIPositve_ratio_of_total_cells")])
```

Pivot the wide count table into tidy long format with `change_data_format_to_longer()`:

```{r qc-step2}
long_df <- change_data_format_to_longer(counts_df)
head(long_df[, c("PID", "Tissue", "Treatment_complete", "Image_number",
                 "marker_positivity", "marker_positivity_ratio")])
```

---

## 2. Patient-Level QC Plots (`get_QC_plots()`)

`get_QC_plots()` displays a trimmed violin density, compact IQR boxplot, and individual field-of-view points for each cell marker, with independent percentage y-axes (`scales = "free_y"`) so low-abundance markers like `cCASP3` are never compressed by high-abundance markers like `E-Cadherin`:

```{r qc-patient-b39}
get_QC_plots(
  long_df,
  isolate_a_specific_patient = "B39",
  save_plots = FALSE
)
```

### Comparing Multiple Doses or Treatments with Statistical Annotations

When a patient has multiple treatments or doses (including a `Control` group), set `compare_to_control = TRUE` to automatically run a Wilcoxon rank-sum test (`stat_method = "wilcox"`) or t-test (`stat_method = "t.test"`) against `Control` within each marker facet:

```{r qc-patient-stats}
get_QC_plots(
  long_df,
  isolate_a_specific_patient = "B39",
  x_plot_var = "Treatment",
  compare_to_control = TRUE,
  control_treatment_name = "Control",
  stat_method = "wilcox",
  p_adjust_method = "BH",
  pvalue_label = "p.adj.signif",
  save_plots = FALSE
)
```

---

## 3. Multi-Condition & Dose QC (`get_QC_plots_parsed_merged_data()`)

`get_QC_plots_parsed_merged_data()` facets by `Treatment` and places all four cell markers side-by-side on the x-axis, with diamonds marking the group mean and horizontal lines marking the median.

### Coloring by Tissue Origin (`fill_color_variable = "Tissue"`)

```{r qc-violin-tissue}
plots_by_tissue <- get_QC_plots_parsed_merged_data(
  long_df,
  list_of_columns_to_plot = "marker_positivity_ratio",
  fill_color_variable = "Tissue",
  isolate_specific_patient = "A8759",
  save_plots = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)

plots_by_tissue[["A8759.marker_positivity_ratio"]]
```

### Coloring by Complete Treatment & Dose (`fill_color_variable = "Treatment_complete"`)

When a drug is tested at multiple concentrations (such as `Paclitaxel` and `NIRAPARIB` from `0.1` to `100` uM), setting `fill_color_variable = "Treatment_complete"` splits the violins by dose within each drug facet:

```{r qc-violin-dose}
plots_by_dose <- get_QC_plots_parsed_merged_data(
  long_df,
  list_of_columns_to_plot = "marker_positivity_ratio",
  fill_color_variable = "Treatment_complete",
  isolate_specific_patient = "B38",
  save_plots = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)

plots_by_dose[["B38.marker_positivity_ratio"]]
```
